# Woney

> Payments infrastructure that gives an AI agent a way to pay that is never its owner's card.

Woney creates a card for each purchase, so an AI agent can pay at any online store on its owner's behalf. The agent shops and checks out the way a person would, and nothing changes on the store's side. It never gets the owner's card, and once a payment goes through, the card it used stops working. The owner decides how much it can spend.

Woney is in private beta and not yet generally available. Access opens in batches from a waitlist at https://woney.ai.

## How it is used

- **Set a limit.** The owner decides how much the agent can spend. It works freely inside that limit and is not asked to approve every purchase.
- **The agent shops.** It searches, compares and pays at any online store, the same way a person would. Nothing changes on the store's side.
- **One card per purchase.** Each purchase gets its own card, for one store and one amount. Once the payment goes through, the card stops working.

## What the card enforces

The limits live in the card itself rather than in instructions the agent is asked to follow.

- One card per purchase, which stops working once the payment goes through
- Each card is created for the exact total of that purchase
- Each card only works at the store it was created for
- The agent buys on its own under the owner's limit; over it, the purchase waits for approval
- A receipt for every purchase, for the agent and for the owner
- A record of who asked, what the agent decided, and which card paid
- The owner's real card is never given to the agent

## How an agent reaches it

An agent reaches Woney through an MCP server or a command-line tool. Both are being built.

## What Woney is not

- **Not a checkout.** The store's checkout is the same page every shopper gets, and the agent works through it exactly as a person would. Woney supplies the card; the buying is the agent's.
- **Not a merchant integration.** Nothing is required of the store.
